segments.text: Mara had not promised to open the gate. She had promised not to open it unless the bell rang three times.
It rang twice. 'Then nobody comes in,' she said. The boy outside did not knock again; he laid a third bell on the snow.
Ilya gave Vera the letter, but she refused to read it aloud. 'If Mother were still alive, she would tell you herself,' Vera said.
He watched her fold the page. It was not the letter he wanted back. It was the voice she had borrowed to say those words.

segments.text: Ash stood beneath the ash tree while the fire settled into ash. The Reed Clan had named him for the tree, not for what remained of the fire.
'I am still here,' he said. No one answered. Still here, he told the empty clearing; still here.
The display read minus 0.4 degrees Celsius. At least twelve seconds had to pass between pulses, and no more than two pulses were allowed before dawn.
'Do not press it unless the window is closed,' Neri said. Sol closed his eyes instead. He had heard every word; he had obeyed none of them.
